sentences.t: A man pushes a shopping cart through a store.
He walks slowly, picks up a few things, and smiles at everyone.
Nobody follows him.
Not one person.
The store owner, Sylvan Goldman, invented that cart himself.
He noticed that his customers only bought what they could carry in a little hand basket.
When the basket got heavy, they stopped shopping and went straight to the register.
So he took a folding chair, put wheels on it, and added two baskets on top.
Problem solved.
Right?
Wait,
what?
Nobody wanted it.
Women said it looked like a baby stroller.
Men said carrying a basket was manly, and pushing a cart was not.
Customers walked right past it.
So he tried something weird.
He hired people to walk around the store, pushing carts, and pretending to shop.
He even paid some of them to stand at the door and show everyone how it works.
And it worked.
Customers saw other people using it,
and thought, Oh, this is normal.
Soon, everybody wanted one.
Sales exploded, and he got rich.
Today, you can't imagine a store without them.
So next time you push a cart, remember:
it only caught on because strangers were paid to make it look normal.
